title: Present Simple – To Be – Review
description: Mixed practice with positive, negative, and question forms of to be

lessons.title: Forms of To Be
lessons.content:
Use **am / is / are** to describe people, things, places, times, and states.

| Subject | To be | Example |
|---------|-------|---------|
| I | am | I am in the office. |
| He / She / It | is | She is my sister. |
| You / We / They | are | They are my friends. |
| Singular noun | is | The party is at 9 o'clock. |
| Plural noun | are | Our parents are at a play. |

📌 Match **to be** to the subject before you choose the answer.

lessons.title: Negative and Yes/No Questions
lessons.content:
For negative sentences, put **not** after **am / is / are**.

| Positive | Negative |
|----------|----------|
| I am a doctor. | I am not a doctor. |
| She is my sister. | She is not my sister. |
| They are at home. | They are not at home. |

For yes/no questions, move **am / is / are** before the subject.

| Sentence | Question |
|----------|----------|
| You are a teacher. | Are you a teacher? |
| The wedding is on Wednesday. | Is the wedding on Wednesday? |
| Our parents are at a play. | Are our parents at a play? |

📌 Common contractions: **is not = isn't**, **are not = aren't**. **I am not** does not usually contract to **amn't**.

lessons.title: WH Questions with To Be
lessons.content:
For WH questions with **to be**, put the question word first, then **am / is / are**, then the subject.

**Structure:** Question word + **am / is / are** + subject + ?

| Answer | Question |
|--------|----------|
| The party is at 8 o'clock. | When is the party? |
| That is a dog. | What is that? |
| They are my cousins. | Who are they? |
| London is in England. | Where is London? |

⚠️ Do not use **do / does** in normal questions with **to be**: **Is he sick?** not **Does he be sick?**
